tools.when_not_to_use: Not to fill in a payment — the number is never returned, so checkout still asks for it. Not for a booking payment state, which is bookings_payment_status.

platform_notes.whatsapp: Check `expired` before ever suggesting a card — an expired one stays in the list and still looks usable, and recommending it produces a decline the customer has to work out for themselves. Never work the expiry out yourself from the date; read the field. The wallet's phone number is NEVER returned, so you cannot fill in a payment from this: name the wallet by its label and let the customer give the number. The default is first in the list.

tools.name: payment_methods_add
tools.title: Save a mobile-money wallet
tools.description: Save a mobile-money wallet so checkout can offer it by name.
tools.when_to_use: From the payment-methods flow only, after the customer has given the number and confirmed the network.
tools.when_not_to_use: There is NO card path and there cannot be one — a card needs the gateway own browser SDK, which a chat does not have. Never ask a customer for card details.

provider.description: The wallet's network. ASK the customer — never infer it from the number.

phoneNumber.description: The wallet's own number, in strict E.164 (for example +237600123456). A locally formatted number is refused at the door rather than saved.

makeDefault.description: Make it the one checkout reaches for first.

errors.when: The number is not strict E.164, or the provider is not one of the three wallets

side_effects: Saves a payment method
makeDefault: true clears the flag on every other method

platform_notes.whatsapp: The label and the last four digits are composed by the backend, not accepted — a label a model wrote could name the wrong network, and that label is what the customer then picks at checkout. E.164 is enforced here because the value is stored as the thing a gateway will later be asked to debit: a locally formatted number saved today is a payment that fails weeks later with nothing to point at.

tools.name: payment_methods_set_default
tools.title: Choose the usual way to pay
tools.description: Make one saved method the one checkout reaches for first.
tools.when_to_use: From the payment-methods flow only, after the customer has named which one.
tools.when_not_to_use: Not to pay with it — this only changes which one is offered first.

methodId.description: The saved method to promote, from payment_methods_list.

errors.when: Not this customer's payment method

side_effects: Clears the default flag on every other saved method

platform_notes.whatsapp: The answer is the WHOLE list rather than the one method, because setting a default clears the flag on every sibling — a single row would leave the caller holding a list it now knows to be stale.

tools.name: payment_methods_remove
tools.title: Forget a saved way to pay
tools.description: Delete one of the customer's saved payment methods.
tools.when_to_use: From the payment-methods flow only, after the customer has named it and confirmed the deletion.
tools.when_not_to_use: Never inferred from "that card does not work any more" without an explicit confirmation.

methodId.description: The saved method to delete, from payment_methods_list.

errors.when: Not this customer's payment method

side_effects: Deletes a saved payment method permanently

platform_notes.whatsapp: Removing the DEFAULT does not elect a replacement — the same rule addresses_remove settled on. hasDefault: false in the answer is the signal to say so, rather than letting the customer find out at checkout.

tools.name: contact_get_state
tools.title: What the account signs in with
tools.description: The email address and phone number the customer signs in with, masked, plus any change that is waiting to be confirmed.
tools.when_to_use: When the customer asks what email or number is on their account, or asks what happened to a change they started.
tools.when_not_to_use: Not for the customer's name, language or addresses — profile_get_summary and addresses_list answer those.

platform_notes.whatsapp: The CURRENT email and number come back MASKED and the field names say so — read emailMasked and phoneMasked, and never present them as the full value. A PENDING change carries its target in full, because the whole point of the read is telling the customer which address to check. If pendingPhone is set, read phoneChangeProved: false means the customer cannot finish that change yet, and the remedy is to connect the new number on WhatsApp first.

tools.name: contact_change_email
tools.title: Start a change of login email
tools.description: Send a confirmation link to a new email address. The address the customer signs in with does not move until that link is opened.
tools.when_to_use: From the contact-change flow only, after the customer has given the new address and confirmed it is right.
tools.when_not_to_use: Never from a sentence like "my email is wrong" alone — this sends real mail to a real address, and a mistyped one is a link nobody will ever open. Ask for the address and read it back first.

email.description: The new email address, exactly as the customer gave it.

errors.when: The address given is the one already on the account
Another account already signs in with that address
The address is not a valid email address

side_effects: Sends a confirmation email to the new address
Replaces any email change already in flight, which invalidates the earlier link

platform_notes.whatsapp: The address the customer signs in with does NOT move here — it moves when the link in the email is opened, on the website. Relay the reply verbatim: it says so, and a customer who believes the change is already done will read the old address still working as a fault. A second call replaces the first, so a mistyped address is corrected by simply giving the right one again.

tools.name: contact_cancel_email_change
tools.title: Abandon a pending email change
tools.description: Cancel an email change that is waiting to be confirmed. Nothing about how the customer signs in changes.
tools.when_to_use: From the contact-change flow only, when the customer has said they no longer want the change they started.
tools.when_not_to_use: Never from "I did not get the email". That is a reason to look in the spam folder or start again with a corrected address — cancelling kills the link that is already sitting in their inbox.

errors.when: There is no email change waiting on this account

side_effects: Invalidates the confirmation link already sent to the new address

platform_notes.whatsapp: This destroys nothing durable — the customer simply starts again — but it does invalidate a link that may already be open in their mail client, so the failure the customer meets next is a link that no longer works. Check with contact_get_state that a change is actually pending before offering this.

tools.name: contact_change_phone
tools.title: Start a change of login phone
tools.description: Record a new phone number for the account. The number the customer signs in with does not move until they prove they control the new one.
tools.when_to_use: From the contact-change flow only, after the customer has given the new number in full international form and confirmed it.
tools.when_not_to_use: Never as a way to fix a wrong number on an order — that is a delivery address, not a login. And never without telling the customer what proving the number involves.

phone.description: The new number in strict international form, for example +237600123456. A locally formatted number is refused at the door rather than saved.

errors.when: The number given is the one already on the account
Another account already signs in with that number
The number is not in strict international form

side_effects: Replaces any phone change already in flight

platform_notes.whatsapp: The number the customer signs in with does NOT move here, and the change usually cannot be finished from this conversation. The only proof the platform accepts is a WhatsApp connection whose number IS the new one, and an account holds at most one WhatsApp connection — so a customer whose WhatsApp is bound to the OLD number has to disconnect it and reconnect from the new one, and a customer on Telegram has to connect WhatsApp for the first time. Relay the reply verbatim: it states that path. Then contact_confirm_phone finishes it.

tools.name: contact_confirm_phone
tools.title: Finish a change of login phone
tools.description: Complete a pending phone change, once the customer has connected the new number on WhatsApp.
tools.when_to_use: From the contact-change flow only, after contact_get_state reports phoneChangeProved: true, or after the customer says they have connected the new number.
tools.when_not_to_use: Not as a retry after a refusal saying the number is not proved yet — nothing changes by asking again. The customer has to connect the number first.

errors.when: There is no phone change waiting on this account
The pending change sat unconfirmed for too long
No WhatsApp connection on this account matches the pending number
Another account claimed that number while the change was pending

side_effects: Moves the number the customer signs in with
Copies the confirmed number onto every role profile the account holds

platform_notes.whatsapp: Takes no arguments — the pending change names the number and the account carries the proof. The number comes back MASKED (phoneMasked), because once it is the account's own identifier it is no longer a value the customer just typed to be checked. A CONTACT_CHANGE_PHONE_UNPROVEN refusal is not a retry: relay its customer message, which names the remedy.

tools.name: contact_cancel_phone_change
tools.title: Abandon a pending phone change
tools.description: Cancel a phone change that is waiting to be confirmed. Nothing about how the customer signs in changes.
tools.when_to_use: From the contact-change flow only, when the customer has said they no longer want the change they started.
tools.when_not_to_use: Never because confirming failed. A change that cannot be proved yet is still the change the customer asked for — cancelling it means starting over.

errors.when: There is no phone change waiting on this account

platform_notes.whatsapp: Cancelling does NOT disconnect anything the customer connected on WhatsApp in order to prove the number — that connection is a separate thing and stays. It only forgets the pending change.

tools.name: connections_list
tools.title: Which messaging apps reach this account
tools.description: Both messaging channels and whether each one is connected to the customer's account, with a hint at the connected identity.
tools.when_to_use: When the customer asks which apps are linked to their account, or before offering to disconnect one.
tools.when_not_to_use: Not for notification preferences — notifications_get_preferences answers which channels the platform may write to.

platform_notes.whatsapp: Always exactly two rows, connected or not — there is no paging and nothing is truncated. identityHint is the ONLY form of the identity that ever comes back; there is no full number or chat id and asking for one will not produce it. isCurrentChannel marks the app this conversation is happening in, which is the one connections_disconnect refuses to cut.

tools.name: connections_disconnect
tools.title: Unlink a messaging app
tools.description: Remove the link between the customer's account and one messaging app.
tools.when_to_use: From the connections flow only, after the customer has named the app and confirmed. Only for the app they are NOT currently writing from.
tools.when_not_to_use: NEVER for the channel this conversation is happening in — it is refused, and it would leave the customer unable to undo it from chat. Never as a way to stop notifications; notifications_update_preferences does that without breaking sign-in.

channel.description: Which messaging app to unlink. Never the one this conversation is happening in.

errors.when: The channel named is the one this request arrived on
That app is not connected to this account

side_effects: The customer can no longer sign in or be recognised from that app until they connect it again
Notifications the platform sent on that channel stop arriving

platform_notes.whatsapp: Read connections_list first and use isCurrentChannel: disconnecting the app this conversation is in is refused, because the customer could not undo it from here. Reconnecting means sending /connect to the bot and redeeming the code while signed in on the website, so this is not a small change to offer casually.

tools.name: account_close_preview
tools.title: What closing the account would do
tools.description: Whether this account can be closed, what would stop it, and the exact sentence describing what closing does — in the customer's language.
tools.when_to_use: Whenever the customer asks about closing or deleting their account, and ALWAYS before account_close. It changes nothing.
tools.when_not_to_use: Not for suspending, pausing or hiding an account — none of those exist. This is the only closure there is.

platform_notes.whatsapp: Relay `consequence` VERBATIM — it is written in the customer's language and it is the sentence they are entitled to read before deciding. Say CLOSED and say that past orders are kept as business records without their details; never say deleted or erased, because that is not what happens. canClose false means it is refused today: blockingRoles non-empty means the account also sells or delivers and support has to handle it, and activeOrderCount above zero means orders are still on the way and closing can happen once they arrive.

tools.name: account_close
tools.title: Close the account
tools.description: Close the customer's account and remove their personal details. Irreversible. Past orders are kept as pseudonymous business records.
tools.when_to_use: From the account-closure flow only, as the SECOND step: account_close_preview first, its consequence shown to the customer, and the customer having confirmed after reading it.
tools.when_not_to_use: Never on a first mention of closing, never inferred from frustration, and never without account_close_preview having been shown. There is no undo and there is no support path to reverse it.

confirm.description: The confirmation token, exactly as account_close_preview returned it in confirmWith. It is an untranslated token, not a sentence the customer types.

errors.when: The account also sells or delivers on the platform
Orders are still on the way
The account is not active — most often because it has already been closed
The confirmation token was missing or wrong

side_effects: Removes the customer's name, contact details, saved addresses and date of birth
Deletes every messaging connection, so this conversation stops being recognised
Deletes saved payment methods and notifications
Past orders and money records are kept, without the customer's details
Irreversible — there is no un-close

platform_notes.whatsapp: This deletes the messaging connection this conversation runs on, so the customer's NEXT message arrives as a stranger. The reply is therefore the last thing the platform says to them as themselves — relay it verbatim. Never describe this as deleting their data or their orders: the orders survive as business records without their name, which is what the reply says and what account_close_preview said before it.

tools.name: reviews_check_eligibility
tools.title: May the customer review this?
tools.description: Whether the customer is allowed to review a product or a delivery — and if not, why.
tools.when_to_use: Before offering to take a review, so an ineligible customer is never asked for one.
tools.when_not_to_use: Not after a failed submission — this is the check that avoids one.

subjectType.description: delivery takes a SHIPMENT id, not an order id.

subjectId.description: The id of the thing being reviewed: a product id when subjectType is product, a SHIPMENT id when it is delivery — never an order id.

platform_notes.whatsapp: A 200 with eligible:false is a successful answer to a question, not a failure. reason is the same code the write path would have raised.

tools.name: reviews_list_mine
tools.title: The reviews the customer wrote
tools.description: The reviews the customer has written themselves, newest first — products and deliveries, in every moderation state.
tools.when_to_use: For "what have I reviewed", "did my review go up", "why can I not see my review", and to check whether they have already rated something.
tools.when_not_to_use: NOT other people's reviews of a product — that is catalog_list_product_reviews.

status.description: Narrow to one moderation state. Leave empty unless the customer asked for one — the default returns all three, which is usually what they mean.

limit.description: At most 5. A chat answer cannot carry more, and the surface refuses a larger value rather than clamping it silently. When more exist, the response reports meta.hasMore and meta.moreUrl — offer that link instead of paging.

errors.when: An unknown status

platform_notes.whatsapp: To say whether a review is visible, read publiclyVisible and NEVER status. A delivery review is stored as status:published and appears on no page anywhere, because it is internal feedback about the carrier — so status alone would have you tell the customer their review is live and send them looking for it. subjectLabel is the product's name; it is null on a delivery review and null on a product no longer for sale, and in that case talk about the order via orderId rather than reading an id aloud. There is no subjectType filter, deliberately: pairing it with status would invite a query whose name promises a page nothing will ever appear on.

tools.name: reviews_create
tools.title: Leave a review
tools.description: Record the customer's rating, and their words if they gave any, about a product they bought or a delivery they received.
tools.when_to_use: Only from the review flow, after eligibility was checked and the customer confirmed what will be published.
tools.when_not_to_use: Never write prose on the customer's behalf, never infer a rating from their tone, and never review a delivery against an order id — the subject is a shipment.

body.description: The customer's own words, verbatim. Optional.

errors.when: Already reviewed
Not completed, not delivered, or a delivered shipment with no agent bound

tools.idempotency: A repeat answers REVIEW_ALREADY_EXISTS.
side_effects: A bare star rating PUBLISHES IMMEDIATELY and moves the product's public rating
A review carrying prose is held for a human moderator
A delivery review is internal, is attributed to the carrying agent server-side, and feeds their trust score

platform_notes.whatsapp: Tell the customer which of the two happens: a rating alone goes live at once, prose waits for a moderator. A delivery review is never published anywhere.

tools.name: notifications_get_preferences
tools.title: How the customer is contacted
tools.description: Which channel the customer gets notifications on and which kinds of update they have switched on.
tools.when_to_use: When the customer asks about the messages they get, or complains about too many or too few.
tools.when_not_to_use: Not to explain a single notification they received — answer the underlying question instead.

platform_notes.whatsapp: At most ONE secondary channel is on at a time; enabling one disables the others. Money messages and cancellations always send and no setting silences them — say so plainly rather than implying everything is switchable.

tools.name: notifications_update_preferences
tools.title: Change how the customer is contacted
tools.description: Switch a kind of update on or off, or move notifications to a different channel.
tools.when_to_use: Only from the notification-settings flow, after confirming exactly what will change.
tools.when_not_to_use: Never in response to 'stop messaging me' alone. Money messages and cancellations cannot be switched off, so silently changing something else answers a request that was not granted.

channel.description: The single secondary channel. Setting one disables the other two.

errors.when: Enabling a channel that is not verified

side_effects: Changes where every future notification is delivered

tools.name: notifications_list
tools.title: The notification inbox
tools.description: The customer's notifications — order progress, payments, bookings, ticket replies — newest first.
tools.when_to_use: When they ask what is new or what they missed, and to work out what a vague reference is about: each row carries subject.type and subject.id, which is exactly what the order or ticket tools want.
tools.when_not_to_use: NOT authoritative for live order status — a notification records one past moment. Read the order.

unreadOnly.description: Set true only if the customer asked specifically for what they have not seen yet. There is deliberately no "read only".

aggregateType.description: Narrow to one subject kind. Leave empty unless the customer named one.

limit.description: At most 5. A chat answer cannot carry more, and the surface refuses a larger value rather than clamping it silently. When more exist, the response reports meta.hasMore and meta.moreUrl — offer that link instead of paging.

errors.when: An aggregateType outside the five customer subjects

platform_notes.whatsapp: meta.unreadCount rides on the response, so "you have N unread" needs no second call. actionUrl is absolute and already in the customer language — relay it as written and never rebuild one. The five aggregate types are derived from the platform own list, so a sixth appearing later is a backend change rather than something to guess at here.

tools.name: notifications_unread_count
tools.title: How many are unread
tools.description: How many notifications the customer has not read — one number.
tools.when_to_use: To answer "anything new?" without pulling a page of rows.
tools.when_not_to_use: Not on every message. It answers a question the customer asked.

platform_notes.whatsapp: A count of zero is a successful answer, not an error. If the customer then asks what they are, notifications_list already reports the same number in meta.unreadCount — so do not call this first as a matter of routine.

tools.name: notifications_mark_read
tools.title: Mark one notification read
tools.description: Mark a single notification as read.
tools.when_to_use: Right after relaying that notification to the customer — reading it aloud to them IS them seeing it.
tools.when_not_to_use: NEVER on a notification you did not show them. There is no way to mark one unread again, so an acknowledgement they did not make cannot be taken back.

notificationId.description: The id of the notification you just showed the customer, from notifications_list.

errors.when: No such notification for this customer — never a 403, so a caller learns nothing about whether the id exists

side_effects: Clears the unread flag, which cannot be set again

platform_notes.whatsapp: One-way: there is no mark-unread route anywhere on this platform. That is why this tool is model-facing while notifications_mark_all_read is not — acknowledging the one you just read out is honest, and doing it to a whole inbox on your own initiative is not.

tools.name: notifications_mark_all_read
tools.title: Acknowledge the whole inbox
tools.description: Mark every one of the customer's notifications as read.
tools.when_to_use: From a deterministic flow step only, when the customer has asked for exactly this.
tools.when_not_to_use: NEVER on a model reading of "yeah I know about those". Nothing can undo it, and the unread flag is how a customer finds what they have not seen.
side_effects: Clears the unread flag on every notification, irreversibly

platform_notes.whatsapp: The answer reports how many rows actually moved, so a flow can say "cleared 4" rather than asserting something it did not measure.

tools.name: payment_create_pay_link
tools.title: Get a page the customer can pay by card on
tools.description: A short-lived link to a page where the customer completes a CARD payment. Mobile money never needs this — it finishes on the customer's handset.
tools.when_to_use: After payment_initiate with gateway STRIPE, when the customer chose to pay by card. Send them the url.
tools.when_not_to_use: Never for mobile money — that completes in the chat and this refuses it. Never for a payment that is already done. If url comes back null the deployment has no payment page: offer mobile money instead.

transactionId.description: The CARD payment’s transaction id, from the payment that was just initiated. Mobile money never needs a link.

errors.when: Unknown id, malformed id, or not the customer's — indistinguishable on purpose
A mobile-money payment, which completes on the handset and needs no page
The payment is already settled, failed or cancelled

tools.notes: A second call REVOKES the first link. Ask for a new one only when the customer says the old one stopped working.

tools.name: messaging_get_window
tools.title: Can I still message this customer in my own words?
tools.description: Whether WhatsApp's 24-hour service window is still open for this customer, and when it closes. Telegram has no such window and always answers open.
tools.when_to_use: Before starting a flow that may finish after the customer stops writing — a payment they will approve later, an order that ships in two days. Decides whether the flow can end in the chat or must hand off to messaging_notify_customer.
tools.when_not_to_use: Not before an ordinary reply. Answering a message the customer just sent is always inside the window.
tools.notes: expiresAt is the platform's own 23-hour window, deliberately earlier than Meta's 24. Read it as 'after this we switch to a template', never as when Meta closes. applicable:false means the channel has no window at all (Telegram).

tools.name: messaging_notify_customer
tools.title: Ask the platform to message the customer for you
tools.description: Hands one situation to the platform to deliver, in the customer's language, through whichever channel reaches them — free-form inside the WhatsApp window, an approved template outside it.
tools.when_to_use: When you have something to tell the customer and cannot send it yourself: the service window has closed, or the flow is ending and the answer comes later. Today the only situation is order.payment_link — a card payment page.
tools.when_not_to_use: Never as a general send. It takes a named situation, never a message you wrote. There is no marketing situation and there will not be one.

situation.description: The closed set of situations the automation layer may raise. One member today.

transactionId.description: The card payment to send a page for. Must be the customer's own.

errors.when: Unknown id, malformed id, or not the customer's — indistinguishable on purpose
A mobile-money payment, or a deployment with no payment page configured
The payment is already settled, failed or cancelled

tools.notes: A 200 means accepted for delivery, not delivered — the platform never fails a business action over a notification. Do not tell the customer a message was sent. This mints a fresh pay link, so it REVOKES any earlier one.
